title: Standardized patient: knee pain
intro: The musculoskeletal encounter: a focused history and knee examination. Door card: Ms. Alicia Moreno, 24, "right knee pain". Twelve minutes.

steps.say: Ms. Moreno sits on the exam table with her right knee propped on a pillow, a pair of crutches against the wall.

options.text: Introduce yourself, confirm her name, and ask what happened.
options.reply: "Hi. Alicia. I did something to my knee playing soccer on Saturday."

options.text: "Let's look at that knee," and reach for it before she's settled.
"Knee pain? On a scale of one to ten?"
options.reply: "Seven? It's more that it gave way." You've jumped past the story.

choice.lesson: Introduce yourself and let the patient tell the story first

history.opening: "I planted my foot to cut past a defender, twisted, and heard a pop. I couldn't keep playing."

items.ask: Did anyone hit your knee, or did it happen on its own?

items.answer: "Within an hour or two it was huge."

items.ask: Could you walk on it afterward?
Does it give way, lock or catch?
items.answer: "It feels wobbly, like it'll give way. It hasn't locked."

items.ask: Any previous knee injuries or surgery?
What have you taken for it?
What do you do, and what do you need the knee for?
items.answer: "I'm a PE teacher. I need to be on my feet all day."

maneuvers.name: Inspect and compare both knees
maneuvers.finding: The right knee is swollen compared with the left, with no bruising or deformity.

maneuvers.name: Palpate for an effusion (patellar tap)
maneuvers.finding: A tense effusion: the patella taps down onto the femur.

maneuvers.name: Range of motion
maneuvers.finding: Flexion limited to 90 degrees by pain and swelling; full extension is possible.

maneuvers.name: Lachman test
maneuvers.finding: Increased forward translation of the tibia with a soft end point compared with the left.

maneuvers.name: Anterior drawer test
maneuvers.finding: Slightly increased translation; guarding limits it.

maneuvers.name: Check pulses and sensation in the foot
maneuvers.finding: Normal dorsalis pedis pulse and sensation.

choice.prompt: She asks, "Is it broken? Will I be able to teach?"

options.text: "I don't think it's broken, but it may be a ligament. The doctor will examine you and talk about imaging and what it means for your work."
options.reply: "OK. Thanks for being straight with me."
She looks relieved, but you can't know that.

options.text: "That's a question for the doctor." Then you leave.

choice.lesson: Answer honestly within your role, without false reassurance

steps.question: sp_knee_dx_01
steps.lead: Your preceptor asks for your impression.

feedback: "Beautiful focused exam, and you always checked the other side and the foot. Well done."
"Good. Always compare with the other knee, and never forget pulses and sensation."
"Let's practice the knee exam sequence together before the practical."
